q: Marginal cost of a product is best defined as:

options.A: Average cost of all units produced
options.B: Additional cost of producing one more unit
options.C: Total fixed cost divided by output

q: Contribution is calculated as:

options.B: Sales minus fixed costs

q: The profit-volume (P/V) ratio is:

options.B: Variable cost divided by sales
options.C: Contribution divided by sales, expressed as a percentage

q: The break-even point is the level of activity where:

options.B: Fixed costs become zero
options.D: Total sales revenue equals total cost

q: Under marginal costing, fixed costs are treated as:

options.A: Absorbed into each unit of output
options.B: Period costs written off against total contribution

q: Under absorption costing, the cost of a product includes:

options.B: Only variable costs
options.C: Variable costs plus a share of fixed manufacturing overhead

q: When production exceeds sales in a period, profit under absorption costing is:

options.B: Lower than under marginal costing

q: Margin of safety is defined as:

options.B: Contribution minus fixed cost

q: A high margin of safety indicates that the business is:

options.B: In a sound position with low risk of loss
options.D: Operating with a low P/V ratio

q: Which of the following will improve the P/V ratio?

options.B: A rise in variable cost per unit
options.C: A rise in selling price with costs unchanged

q: Break-even point in units is equal to:

options.A: Fixed costs divided by contribution per unit
options.B: Fixed costs divided by variable cost per unit
options.C: Sales divided by contribution per unit
options.D: Profit divided by contribution per unit

q: Break-even sales value is calculated as:

options.A: Fixed cost multiplied by P/V ratio
options.B: Contribution divided by fixed cost
options.C: Variable cost divided by P/V ratio
options.D: Fixed cost divided by P/V ratio

q: Sunk costs are costs that:

options.B: Have already been incurred and cannot be changed
options.C: Will be incurred in the future

q: In a make-or-buy decision, the relevant cost of making in-house is the:

options.A: Marginal cost plus any avoidable fixed cost of manufacture
options.B: Total cost including apportioned general overheads

q: A special order below normal selling price should be accepted when:

options.A: It covers the full absorption cost
options.B: Total profit of the firm falls
options.C: Price exceeds marginal cost and spare capacity exists

q: The key (limiting) factor in a product-mix decision is:

options.A: Total fixed cost of the workshop
options.B: The selling price of the products
options.D: The scarcest resource that constrains output

q: When a key factor exists, products should be ranked on the basis of:

options.B: Contribution per unit of the key factor

q: Opportunity cost is best defined as:

options.A: The benefit forgone in the next best alternative use
options.B: The actual cash paid for a resource
options.C: The historical cost of an asset
options.D: Fixed cost per unit of output

q: Differential cost refers to:

options.B: The fixed cost of a department
options.C: The difference in total cost between two alternatives
options.D: Variable cost of the last unit

q: A workshop choosing between in-house repair and an outside contract should ignore:

options.A: Future material cost of the repair
options.B: Labour cost of the repair work
options.D: Book value of the machine already purchased

q: The shut-down point is reached when:

options.A: Profit is at its maximum level
options.B: Contribution just covers avoidable fixed costs

q: Which statement about marginal costing is correct?

options.B: Profit is distorted by changes in stock
options.C: Fixed costs are not carried forward in stock valuation
options.D: It is required for external financial reporting

q: The P/V ratio can also be expressed as:

options.A: Change in profit divided by change in sales
options.B: Change in sales divided by change in profit

q: In deciding whether to repair or scrap a wagon, the relevant comparison is between:

options.A: Original cost of the wagon and scrap value
options.B: Book value of the wagon and repair cost
options.C: Total historical cost and replacement cost
options.D: Marginal cost of repair and net scrap proceeds

q: Margin of safety can be improved by:

options.B: Reducing variable cost per unit

q: Under marginal costing, closing stock is valued at:

options.B: Full absorption cost

q: Which cost is relevant when accepting an order that uses idle capacity?

options.B: Depreciation on existing plant
options.C: Incremental variable cost of the order

q: A rise in fixed costs, with other factors unchanged, will:

options.B: Improve the P/V ratio
options.C: Leave the margin of safety unchanged

q: In a continue-or-shut-down decision, which fixed costs are relevant?

options.B: All apportioned fixed costs

q: For POH versus replacement of a coach, the correct approach compares:

options.A: Original cost of the coach with the new coach price
options.B: Marginal cost of POH plus future running costs against replacement cost
options.C: Book value of the coach with its scrap value
options.D: Total past maintenance with the new coach price

q: When sales exceed production in a period, profit under marginal costing is:

options.B: Equal to absorption costing profit

q: Contribution per unit is equal to:

options.A: Fixed cost per unit plus profit
options.B: Selling price minus fixed cost
options.D: Selling price minus variable cost per unit

q: A product should be discontinued when its:

options.B: Sales are falling

q: The main advantage of marginal costing for short-term decisions is that it:

options.A: Spreads fixed costs fairly over products
options.B: Focuses on incremental costs and contribution

q: Which of the following is a limitation of marginal costing?

options.A: It values stock at variable cost
options.B: It ignores contribution
options.C: It is useful for pricing decisions
options.D: It suits short-term rather than long-term decisions

q: In make-or-buy analysis, if the supplier's price is below the marginal cost of manufacture:

options.B: Let fixed costs alone decide
options.C: Buying is cheaper, subject to quality and reliability
options.D: Add apportioned overhead to the buy price

q: Differential costing is most useful for:

options.A: Choosing between alternative courses of action
options.B: Valuing closing stock

q: An increase in selling price with no change in costs will:

options.B: Lower the break-even point
options.D: Leave the margin of safety unchanged

q: Which cost should be ignored when deciding to replace an old machine?

options.A: Operating cost of the new machine
options.B: Disposal value of the old machine
options.C: Maintenance cost of the old machine
options.D: Written-down book value of the old machine

q: On a break-even chart, the break-even point is shown where:

options.A: The fixed cost line meets the sales line
options.B: The variable cost line meets the x-axis
options.C: The total cost line intersects the sales revenue line
options.D: The contribution line meets the y-axis

q: If fixed costs rise and the same profit is desired, the firm must:

options.A: Increase contribution by the same amount
options.B: Reduce variable costs to zero

q: Under marginal costing, an increase in closing stock will:

options.B: Leave reported profit unaffected by the stock change

q: In a special-order decision, the minimum acceptable price in the short run is:

options.B: Normal selling price

q: Which pair correctly matches the costing method with stock valuation?

options.B: Absorption costing with variable cost only
options.C: Marginal costing with variable cost only
options.D: Both value stock at selling price

q: A workshop with idle labour hours should accept extra work if the price covers:

options.A: The variable cost of the extra work
options.B: A share of total fixed overheads
options.D: The full cost plus normal profit

q: The angle of incidence in a break-even chart indicates:

options.B: The rate at which profit is earned above break-even

q: Under a single limiting factor, the most profitable product mix gives priority to:

options.A: The product with the highest selling price
options.B: The product with the highest total profit
options.C: Producing all products in equal quantities
options.D: The highest contribution per unit of the limiting factor

q: Which of the following is an example of a relevant cost?

options.A: Depreciation on a fully installed machine
options.B: Allocated head-office rent
options.C: Extra material needed for a special order

q: A key factor is also known as:

options.B: The fixed cost

q: For short-term workshop decisions, marginal costing is preferred because it:

options.B: Is required by company law
options.D: Avoids arbitrary apportionment of fixed overheads
